{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Development and Option Agreement

**Prepared by:** In-house counsel (for Customer / AbbVie)  
**Subject:** Playbook review findings — Development and Option Agreement (Harpoon)

---

## Executive summary

We have reviewed the Agreement against the playbook. The overall risk allocation is favourable to us: the licence grant to us is exclusive, sublicensable through multiple tiers and becomes irrevocable on expiry of the Term (§§ 5.1.3, 5.3, 12.1.2); we hold an unrestricted termination-for-convenience right on 90 days' notice with no exit fee (§ 12.3); Harpoon carries the exclusivity/non-compete burden (§ 5.8); and we are subject to no non-compete, non-solicit, MFN, minimum-volume or liquidated-damages obligation. Ownership of IP, Regulatory Documentation and Regulatory Approvals sits with us where it matters (§§ 3.8.2(c), 7.1.1), and Harpoon's indemnity in our favour (§ 11.2) carries the standard procedural protections and covers third-party IP infringement claims (§ 7.4).

Two items require attention:

1. **Limitation of liability (deviation, high).** Section 11.5 excludes indirect and consequential damages but contains **no monetary cap of any kind** on either party's direct liability. This fails both our preferred position and the fallback (mutual cap at 12 months' fees), so we propose a redline.
2. **Forum (needs review, medium).** Delaware governing law is acceptable at the fallback (§ 13.6.1), but the arbitral seat and rules sit in Schedule 13.7.3, which is redacted. Because an arbitration seated outside the U.S. is walk-away territory, we cannot clear this without the Schedule.

We also flag redacted figures ([***]) in the indemnity triggers (§§ 11.1–11.2), audit parameters (§ 6.11) and insurance limits (§ 11.6) that should be confirmed against the unredacted execution copy. These are verification points, not deviations.

---

## Findings

| Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Compliant | § 11 (Indemnity) | Harpoon indemnity in our favour with standard procedure (§§ 11.2–11.5); third-party IP claims in scope via § 7.4. Redacted triggers to confirm. |
| Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Compliant | § 7 (Intellectual Property) | Each party retains its own IP (§ 7.1.1); we solely own Regulatory Documentation and Approvals (§ 3.8.2(c)); Harpoon's licence to our IP is narrow (§ 5.2). |
| High | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability | **Deviation** | § 11 (Indemnity), § 11.5 | No monetary cap on direct liability anywhere in the document; fails the fallback on a material term. Redline proposed. |
| High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Compliant | § 13.2.2 / § 13.4.1 | Symmetrical affiliate and successor carve-out; other assignments subject to reasonableness consent. Change-of-control machinery runs only against Harpoon. |
| High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | Compliant | § 5 (Grant of Rights) | Section 5.8 exclusivity binds Harpoon, not us; § 4.5.1 gives us a right, not an obligation, to manufacture/supply. |
| High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Compliant | § 5 (Grant of Rights) | Exclusive grant, multi-tier sublicensing (§ 5.3), irrevocable post-Term (§ 12.1.2), binding on successors (§ 13.4.1). |
| High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete on Customer | Compliant | § 5 (Grant of Rights) | No non-compete, exclusivity or field-of-use covenant restricts our business; Field/Territory limits are grant-scope only. |
| High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Compliant | § 12 (Term and Termination), § 12.3 | Termination for any or no reason on 90 days' notice, in whole or country-by-country; no exit fee. Harpoon has no convenience right. |
| High | LD — Liquidated damages / penalties on Customer | Compliant | § 12 (Term and Termination) | No liquidated damages, termination fee or acceleration; § 6.10 late interest is mutual and compensatory. |
| Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | **Needs review** | § 13.4.2 / §§ 13.6–13.7 | Delaware law sits at the fallback; arbitral seat and rules are in redacted Schedule 13.7.3. IP validity disputes carved out to court (§ 13.7.2); interim relief preserved (§ 13.7.5). |
| Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Compliant | § 6.5.3 / § 6.11 | Limited to royalty books and records, independent accountant reasonably acceptable to us, capped frequency, Harpoon-borne cost, confidentiality (§ 6.13). Redacted frequency, notice and variance threshold to confirm. |
| Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation obligations | Compliant | § 6 (Payments and Records) | No MFN or best-terms obligation on us; § 5.9.3 is an option in our favour. |
| Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase commitments | Compliant | § 4 (Commercialization) | No minimum, take-or-pay, shortfall or volume construct; § 4.5.1 confers a right, not an obligation. |
| Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | Compliant | § 13 (Miscellaneous) | No solicitation, hire, recruit or inducement covenant anywhere in the Agreement. |
| Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and notice window | Compliant | § 12 (Term and Termination) | Fixed, event-based Term; no evergreen renewal, notice window or renewal uplift. |
| Medium | TRANSITION — Post-termination transition and data return | Compliant (at fallback) | § 12 (Term and Termination) | Developed exit architecture (§§ 12.6–12.8, 12.10.2), bankruptcy access to licensed IP (§ 12.5.2); inbound transition secured in-Term (§§ 4.5.2–4.5.3). |
| Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Compliant | § 10 (Representations and Warranties) | Substantial Harpoon warranty package (§ 10.2) plus performance covenants (§§ 3.8.4, 10.3.3); § 10.5 disclaimer expressly carves back express warranties. |
| Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Compliant (at/above fallback) | § 11 (Indemnity), § 11.6 | Workers' comp, employer's liability, general liability including Clinical Trial Insurance, A- VII carriers, additional insured, certificates, tail cover. Redacted limits to confirm. |

---

## Walk-away items

No walk-away trigger is confirmed on the face of the document. One potential trigger remains open:

- **Arbitral seat (§ 13.7.3 / Schedule 13.7.3).** Arbitration seated outside the United States is walk-away territory under our playbook. The Schedule is redacted, so the seat is unverified. This is a condition to clearance rather than a present walk-away.

---

## Next steps

1. **Limitation of liability — issue redline.** Add a single mutual aggregate cap sentence to § 11.5 at the greater of 12 months' payments by AbbVie and USD 1,000,000, leaving the indemnity, confidentiality, gross negligence, willful misconduct, fraud and IP-infringement carve-outs uncapped (mirroring the exceptions already agreed in § 11.5), and confirming that our Article 6 payment obligations are not capped "damages".
2. **Obtain Schedule 13.7.3** and confirm a U.S. seat (preferably New York, Delaware or California). If the seat falls outside the accepted list, we would redline the seat only and leave Delaware governing law intact. We also note that § 13.6 is captioned "Governing Law, Jurisdiction and Service" but contains no express submission-to-jurisdiction provision, while § 13.6.2 refers to service "in any such court" — worth aligning once the forum is fixed.
3. **Confirm redacted figures against the unredacted execution copy and disclosure schedules:**
   - §§ 11.1–11.2 indemnity triggers (breadth of Harpoon's coverage; narrowness of our reciprocal indemnity);
   - § 6.11 audit frequency, notice and variance threshold (target: once per 12 months, 15–30 days' notice, threshold no lower than 5%);
   - §§ 11.6.1(b)–(c) insurance limits and § 11.6.2 tail period;
   - closing proviso of § 7.1.2 and the redacted parts of § 12.7.1.
4. **Preserve terms that favour us** and resist reciprocal tightening in later drafts: Harpoon's § 5.8 exclusivity and our associated information-cut-off and JGC rights; our § 12.3 convenience right; our § 11.6.3 self-insurance right; and the absence of any non-compete, non-solicit, MFN or minimum-commitment obligation on us. If a non-solicit is introduced, our fallback is services personnel only, 12 months, with general-advertising and unsolicited-approach carve-outs and no no-hire.

*Nothing in this memo reflects a review of terms not covered by the findings above.*"}
